title: feat: track referral visitor login status
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds signed-in / signed-out status at arrival to existing referral analytics, including the low-balance links from #14700. Sends no user IDs and does not compare visitors with API-key owners.
- Stores `logged_in` in a JSON-string `metadata` column so additional properties need no new columns. Historical events default to `{}`; failed session lookups store `logged_in: null`. Both mean unknown, not signed out.
- Reads the browser session in the existing background task without refreshing it. Links and frontend behavior stay unchanged.
- Validates signed-in, signed-out, expired-session, API-key-only, and unknown-ref cases: all 9 tests pass, plus type check and Biome. The earlier local staging build passed; no live staging deployment or end-to-end staging test has been performed.
- Requires the Tinybird datasource update in staging and production before Worker rollout.

gist.headline: The garden counts arrivals
gist.blurb: Referral links now carry a little more context into the hive: whether a visitor arrived signed in, signed out, or as an unknown. No identities collected, just healthier trail markers.
gist.summary: Referral analytics now store a privacy-preserving `logged_in` arrival status in JSON `metadata`, including low-balance referral links, with `null` or empty metadata representing unknown session state.
gist.impact: Maintainers can distinguish signed-in and signed-out referral arrivals without recording user IDs, matching visitors to API-key owners, refreshing browser sessions, or changing referral-link behavior.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a tiny garden surveyor marking anonymous visitor trails on a cozy referral-path map. A retro terminal shows simple status symbols—signed-in, signed-out, and a question mark for unknown—while flowers and code-plants grow beside the paths, emphasizing useful aggregate context rather than personal identity.
